input.quote: Thereafter, this Agreement shall automatically renew for subsequent one (1) year periods unless either party provides the other party with written notification at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the initial five (5) year term or any one (1) year renewal thereof of its intention to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty or minimum-fee-on-termination obligation payable by Corio (the licensee/customer). Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalt", "minimum" and late-payment interest return nothing relevant: the fee provisions (§4.1-4.4, Exhibit B pricing and Exhibit B payment terms) impose only ordinary license, maintenance, revenue-share and implementation fees with no accelerated or penal sums; §11.1 permits termination on 30 days' notice at the end of the initial term or any renewal with no early-termination or wind-down fee; §11.2 allows termination for uncured material breach without any pre-agreed damages amount; §11.3 continues only payment obligations for Corio's then-existing customers and ongoing maintenance fees if Corio elects to keep support. §9 caps each party's liability at amounts actually paid by Corio and excludes consequential damages, which further precludes penal recovery. This sits at the playbook's preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer), so no redline is required. Note only that the audit provision (§4.4) requires Corio to reimburse audit costs where an underpayment exceeds 5% — a cost-shifting mechanic, not a penalty or liquidated damages, and not flagged.
